name: Montenegro
summary: Montenegro (euro, non-EU) taxes residents' worldwide capital gains at a flat 15% (no municipal surtax on gains) and dividends at 15% plus a municipal surtax of up to 15% of the tax (17.25% in Podgorica). No wealth tax, and no inheritance or gift tax for children (only real estate transfer tax for other heirs). No special tax regime for wealthy arrivals.

regimes.name: Ordinary tax residence
regimes.eligibility: Tax resident if domiciled, centre of vital interests in Montenegro, or 183+ days in the tax year. Non-citizens need a residence permit.

capital_gains.summary: Resident individuals pay a flat 15% personal income tax on capital gains from shares, securities and real estate, worldwide. Gain = sale price minus acquisition price. No holding-period exemption for securities. The municipal surtax (prirez) is not charged on capital-gains tax: the Law on Financing Local Self-Government (Art. 8(3)) levies it only on the tax on personal earnings, self-employment income, income from property and property rights, and capital income (dividends, interest).
capital_gains.exemptions_thresholds: Exempt: sale of the taxpayer's only and main residence; transfers between spouses linked to marriage, divorce or inheritance; gifts to first-order relatives (spouse, children). Capital losses can be set against gains of the same year.
capital_gains.eligibility_conditions: Tax residents (domicile, centre of vital interests, or 183+ days) are taxed on worldwide gains.
capital_gains.regional_differences: PIT is national. The municipal surtax does not apply to capital gains (Law on Financing Local Self-Government, Sl. list CG 3/2019, Art. 8(3) lists the taxes it is levied on, and capital gains are not among them).
capital_gains.important_exceptions: Since Sl. list CG 152/22 (in force 30 Dec 2022) capital, capital-gains and property income is taxed at 15% (previously 9%). The tax authority can substitute market value when shares in a company are sold below market value.

open_questions: Current consolidated text of the PIT law after Sl. list CG 152/22 and later amendments could not be opened; the 15% rate relies on PwC (reviewed Aug 2026) and Unija/ePorezi summaries.
No exit tax for individuals was found, but this was not confirmed against legislation.
The surtax conclusion rests on the 2019 text of the local-finance law (Paragraf, last updated 2021); later amendments were not checked.
capital_gains.rate_basis: Flat 15% PIT rate on net capital gains (law amended by Sl. list CG 152/22). No municipal surtax: Art. 8(3) of the local-finance law does not list tax on capital gains in the surtax base.
capital_gains.professional_trader: Frequent trading could be treated as self-employment (entrepreneurial) income, taxed at progressive 0/9/15% plus social contributions; no specific guidance found.
capital_gains.holding_period_rules: No holding-period exemption for shares or real estate (other than the main-residence exemption).
capital_gains.foreign_assets: Worldwide taxation for residents with a foreign tax credit capped at Montenegrin tax; treaties prevail.

dividends.summary: Dividends received by resident individuals are capital income taxed at a flat 15% on the gross amount, withheld by a Montenegrin payer; foreign dividends are self-assessed at 15% with a credit for foreign tax up to the Montenegrin tax. The municipal surtax applies on top, because Art. 8(3) of the Law on Financing Local Self-Government includes the tax on capital income in its base: up to 15% of the tax in Podgorica and Cetinje (15% x 1.15 = 17.25%), up to 13% elsewhere (16.95%).
dividends.exemptions_thresholds: Interest on bonds of the State, the Central Bank or local governments is not taxable capital income (from 19 Nov 2025, Sl. list CG 133/25).
dividends.regional_differences: Municipal surtax on the tax on capital income, set by each municipality: up to 15% in Podgorica (Glavni grad) and Cetinje (Prijestonica), up to 13% elsewhere (Art. 8(1)–(2)). Effective 17.25% in Podgorica; the Tivat and Budva rates were not checked (at most 16.95%).
dividends.important_exceptions: Pre-2023 rate was 9%; some secondary sources still quote 9%.

open_questions: Surtax rates actually set by Tivat and Budva not checked; the JSON uses the Podgorica maximum.
Whether the surtax is collected on self-assessed foreign dividends in practice (the law applies it to the tax on capital income generally).
Mechanics of self-assessment for foreign dividends received through a foreign broker.
dividends.rate_basis: 15% PIT on gross dividends (PwC, reviewed 7 Aug 2026) plus the Podgorica municipal surtax of 15% of the tax (local-finance law Art. 8): 0.15 x 1.15 = 0.1725.
dividends.withholding_outbound: 15% WHT on dividends paid to residents and non-residents (30% to entities in listed tax havens), reducible by treaty.
dividends.treaty_network: 47 treaties per PwC, including most EU states, UK, Switzerland, UAE, China; no treaty with the United States.
dividends.holding_company_notes: Corporate shareholders: dividends from resident companies are generally excluded from the CIT base; not researched in depth.

wealth_tax.summary: Montenegro has no net wealth tax and no recurring levy on financial assets.

wealth_tax.property_tax_note: Annual real estate tax at municipal rates of 0.25%-1% of market value (PwC). A 2025 amendment to the real estate tax law was enacted; its detail was not reviewed.

inheritance.summary: There is no inheritance or gift tax on money, securities or other movables. Inherited or gifted real estate is subject to real estate transfer tax (3%/5%/6% progressive), but first-order heirs (children, spouse) and the deceased's parents, and first-order donees and the donor's spouse, are exempt.
inheritance.exemptions_thresholds: Art. 14(1)(1) Law on Real Estate Transfer Tax: no tax for the first-order heir, spouse and parent of the deceased, or a first-order donee and the donor's spouse.
inheritance.eligibility_conditions: Exemption depends on the family relationship only.
inheritance.important_exceptions: Other heirs pay real estate transfer tax: 3% up to EUR 150,000, 5% EUR 150,000-500,000, 6% above (since 1 Jan 2024). Gifts to first-order relatives are also exempt from capital gains tax.

open_questions: Exemption article taken from the 2013 consolidated text; a 2026 secondary source confirms it is unchanged, but the current official consolidated text was not opened.
Montenegrin real estate held by a foreign estate and probate/court fees were not quantified.
inheritance.gift_tax: No gift tax on movables; real estate gifts follow real estate transfer tax with the same first-order exemption.
inheritance.business_relief: Not needed for children; no tax on shares.
inheritance.foreign_assets: Transfer tax applies only to real estate located in Montenegro.
inheritance.spouse_note: No tax on movables; the spouse of the deceased is exempt from real estate transfer tax on inherited real estate (Law on Real Estate Transfer Tax, Art. 14(1)(1)).

residency.tax_residency_test: Resident if domicile or centre of personal and economic interests in Montenegro, or present at least 183 days in a tax year; treaty tie-breakers prevail.

routes.name: Temporary residence permit (e.g. real estate ownership, business, family)
routes.requirements: Montenegro is not in the EU; all foreigners including EU citizens need a residence permit. Grounds and conditions (including the property-ownership ground) not verified for 2026. The citizenship-by-investment programme closed at the end of 2022 (not re-verified).

corporate.summary: Progressive CIT: 9% up to EUR 100,000 profit, 12% to EUR 1.5m, 15% above. No municipal CIT. 15% WHT on dividends (30% to tax havens).

prime_rent_monthly.description: Median asking rent of 177 long-term house rentals in Podgorica city with 4-6 bedrooms and at least 180 m2 (range EUR 300-5,000; first quartile EUR 1,500, third quartile EUR 3,000; median area 250 m2) in Donja Gorica, Gornja Gorica, Gorica C, Tolosi, Stari Aerodrom, Zlatica, Zabjelo, Zagoric and other city districts, parsed from all 29 result pages of Realitica's Montenegro long-term house rentals filtered on 'Podgorica' (714 results) on 2026-10-15. Agency listings may repeat; asking prices on a listing portal. Replaces the Tivat (Porto Montenegro) figure of EUR 4,500, which is a marina enclave.

intl_school_annual_fee.description: Knightsbridge Schools International, Porto Montenegro, Tivat (IB): IB Diploma Programme EUR 22,320 a year (MYP EUR 20,400), as published on the fee page on 2026-10-15 (the school publishes the next year's fees by 30 April, so taken as 2026/27). One-off: EUR 800 registration and EUR 3,200 capital levy.

cost_of_living.notes: Rent is for Podgorica, the capital. The international school fee is for Tivat (Porto Montenegro), the only IB school found; Podgorica has no comparable figure here. Health insurance and housekeeper costs not sourced.

us_citizen_notes: No US-Montenegro income tax treaty; US citizens rely on US foreign tax credits for Montenegrin 15% tax.
